items.q: Match each haemostatic variable with the direction printed for it in the causes of thrombosis — 1) Antithrombin III and protein C/S 2) Fibrinogen 3) Plasminogen … A) Lost in urine B) Increased C) Decreased D) Unchanged
items.exp: The block reads: loss of antithrombin III in urine, loss of protein C,S in urine, ↑platelet aggregation, ↑fibrinogen and ↓plasminogen. (Book p758)

items.q: A child with steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome has serum albumin 1.4 g/dL and suddenly passes cola-coloured urine with left loin pain. The page's warning that fits best is:
opts: Renal vessel thrombosis, a risk once serum albumin falls below 2 g/dL
Pneumococcal peritonitis, the m/c cause of death
items.exp: Under Risk of thrombosis the page states: if serum albumin <2 g/dl → can lead to renal vessel thrombosis, CVT, DVT; loin pain with macroscopic haematuria in a hypoalbuminaemic nephrotic child is the classic presentation. (Book p758)
